newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mortar bomb blasts heard in Zairean city of Bukavu.
newsitem.headline: Mortar bomb blasts heard in Zairean city of Bukavu.

text.p: Four mortar bomb blasts were heard from the southern edges of the eastern Zairean city of Bukavu on Saturday as militiamen prepared to defend it against rebels.
Reuters photographer Corinne Dufka heard the blasts from the area near Panzi camp, 10 km (six miles) south of the city centre, but it was unclear if the fire was incoming or outgoing.
Zairean troops have been pulling back towards Bukavu, capital of South Kivu province, in the last few days as ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels advance from the south.
It was the first time mortar explosions had been clearly audible in Bukavu since fighting broke out more than a week ago.
"We went towards the south of the city and militiamen had blocked the roads and civilians started stoning journalists," Dufka said.
"We then saw more than 100 militiamen, youths armed only with pieces of wood, who had been rounded up to defend the city. They have been running around in gangs all morning," she added.
Panzi camp houses 2,000 former Hutu soldiers of the Rwandan army and 5,000 family members who fled into Zaire in fear of reprisals for the genocide in Rwanda in 1994.
